steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Statistical Enquiry Cycle (SEC) is a structured approach to carrying out a statistical investigation.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The five/six stages are: Plan, Collect, Process, Present, Interpret and Evaluate.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Some specifications list five stages (combining Interpret and Evaluate); others list six.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Plan: Define the hypothesis, identify variables, decide on methods and sample.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: List the stages of the Statistical Enquiry Cycle in order. | Q: At which stage would you calculate the mean and range of a data set? | Q: At which stage would you draw a scatter graph to show the relationship between two variables?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Plan, Collect, Process, Present, Interpret, Evaluate. | Process. | Present.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Learn the stages in order — exam questions often ask you to name or sequence them. When asked which stage an action belongs to, think about what the action achieves. Calculating statistics is 'Process'; drawing a chart is 'Present'; writing a conclusion is 'Interpret'. Evaluation questions are common — always comment on bias, sample size and method. Remember the cycle can be iterative — evaluation leads to improvement and re-planning.
